headline: Results of First General Meeting

summary: European Opportunities Trust PLC announced that shareholders passed two resolutions at its First General Meeting on 28 July 2026 with 99.98% approval. The resolutions approved reclassification of shares into A, B, and C categories and implementation of a scheme of reconstruction and members' voluntary winding up under section 110 of the Insolvency Act 1986. Voting was 18,625,326 votes for and 4,340 against (representing 39.93% ISC). Assets will be allocated to liquidation, cash, JEGI rollover, and LEO rollover pools, with trading suspended from 29 July and share reclassification occurring 6 August 2026.

The Association maintains strong liquidity with £38m available resources and comfortable covenant headroom, with EBITDA interest cover at 193% against a 130% golden rule threshold and 120% covenant requirement.
retail_take: Solid operational performance with improving margins, cost control and robust financial position; demonstrates resilience in affordable housing sector with strong covenant headroom suggesting low financial distress risk.

headline: Half-year Report
brief: ASCoT reports 5.5% NAV total return for H1 2026, significantly outperforming its 1.8% benchmark despite Iran war impact and AI-driven market volatility.
summary: Aberforth Smaller Companies Trust delivered net asset value total return of 5.5% in the six months to 30 June 2026, substantially outperforming the DNSCI (XIC) benchmark at 1.8%. Net assets stood at £1,391m. The interim dividend increased 7.0% to 15.30p per share. The portfolio benefited from gearing (5.4% ratio) and share buybacks (2.3m shares repurchased at 10.3% average discount). Management fees were reduced effective 1 January 2026, saving approximately £250,000 annually. The period was marked by geopolitical disruption from the Iran war and AI-driven sector rotations.
retail_take: Strong outperformance in a difficult environment, combined with growing dividends, fee reductions, and active capital management through buybacks, presents a compelling story for income-focused investors in small-cap UK equities despite macro headwinds.

headline: 2nd Quarter Financial Results
brief: Boeing Q2 2026: $24.6bn revenue, 171 deliveries, record $715bn backlog despite continued losses.
summary: Boeing reported Q2 2026 revenue of $24.6 billion (up 8% YoY) with 171 commercial aircraft deliveries. The company posted a GAAP loss per share of $0.67 and core loss per share of $0.76, but generated $1.4 billion operating cash flow and $0.6 billion free cash flow. Total backlog reached a record $715 billion including over 6,200 commercial airplanes. The 737 program transitioned to 47/month production rate with 737-7 and 737-10 certification flight testing completed; both variants expected to certify in 2026 with first deliveries in 2027. 777X received FAA approval for certification flight testing with first delivery anticipated in 2027. Defense, Space & Security revenue grew 13% to $7.5 billion but operating margins fell to -0.2% due to $280 million in VC-25B program losses.
retail_take: Strong recovery trajectory with record backlog and positive cash flow momentum offset by persistent losses and program challenges; market likely reads as cautious optimism on operational turnaround despite financial headwinds.

headline: Half-year Results
brief: Hongkong Land reports 11% underlying profit growth to US$259m in H1 2026, with NAV per share up 3% and interim dividend increased to US¢8.0.

retail_take: Positive read: double-digit profit growth, successful capital recycling reducing leverage, third-party capital platform launch, and upgraded FY guidance suggest execution on strategic transformation, though China weakness and lower free cash flow provide some offset.

GSK will vacate its Stevenage site with phased moves by 2029 and upgrade Ware facilities for drug development and manufacturing. London headquarters remains unaffected. GSK invests £6 billion annually in R&D, over £1.5 billion in the UK.
retail_take: Long-term positive signal: substantial UK investment demonstrates confidence in R&D pipeline acceleration and collaboration potential, offsetting transition costs and Stevenage closure disruption. Supports growth strategy in oncology, respiratory, vaccines and HIV.

brief: GSK reports strong Q2 core results with 7% core operating profit growth; reaffirms 2026 guidance and announces £1.9bn cost-saving programme.

A three-year £1.9bn annual cost-saving programme targets 2029 realisation to fund R&D acceleration and a new flagship Cambridge R&D centre. headline: Trading Update
brief: NIOX Group reports H1 2026 revenue of £24.0m, slightly down on prior year, with strong gross margins and net cash of £16.8m.
summary: NIOX Group's clinical revenue reached £20.6m (H1 2025: £20.0m) while research revenue declined to £3.4m from £5.2m due to strategic inventory prioritisation. Revenue fell to £24.0m from £25.2m year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA decreased to £8.3m from £9.2m, though gross margin improved to 71%. The company maintains net cash of £16.8m after paying a £6.5m dividend and expects to return excess capital in H2 2026. Full-year trading remains on track with consensus expectations (£50.5m revenue, £17.5m adjusted EBITDA). NIOX PRO® received CE Mark and UK MHRA approval; US and Japan approvals anticipated in H2 2026.
retail_take: Mixed signals: H1 revenue decline offset by margin improvement, strong balance sheet, and H2 catalysts (NIOX PRO® rollout, Japan pricing increase, US approvals) supporting full-year guidance and shareholder returns.

headline: Vesting of Share Option Award
brief: DSW Capital Executive Director James Dow's share options partially vested; 46,933 of 221,629 options granted in August 2022 meet performance conditions.
summary: The Remuneration Committee completed its assessment of performance conditions on James Dow's August 2022 share option award. Of 221,629 options granted, 46,933 vested following partial satisfaction of performance conditions. The vested options will be satisfied through existing Employee Benefit Trust shares with no new issuance, avoiding shareholder dilution. The vesting occurred on 27 July 2026.
retail_take: Routine PDMR disclosure indicating partial performance condition achievement; vesting through existing shares eliminates dilution concerns. Non-event for investors as execution mechanics appear orderly and aligned with stated policy.

headline: Current £175m share buyback increased to £250m
brief: Inchcape increases share buyback programme from £175m to £250m, signalling board confidence in future prospects.
summary: Inchcape PLC has expanded its share buyback programme by £75m to £250m total, announced alongside H1 2026 results. The increase, covering up to 53.6m shares, reflects strong free cash flow and balance sheet strength. UBS will manage the non-discretionary programme through 5 March 2027, with purchases made via open market transactions. Purchased shares will be cancelled to reduce capital.
retail_take: Demonstrates management confidence and disciplined capital allocation, typically viewed positively by markets as evidence of strong cash generation and shareholder-friendly capital deployment.

headline: Appointment of Chief Financial Officer
brief: Forterra appoints Lisa Oxnard as CFO, replacing Ben Guyatt who departs 31 October 2026.
summary: Lisa Oxnard joins Forterra as Chief Financial Officer and Executive Director later in 2026, following Ben Guyatt's announced departure on 31 October 2026. Oxnard brings 25+ years' international finance and operational leadership experience across manufacturing and industrial businesses, including previous CFO roles at JELD-WEN Europe and Doncasters Group, and currently serves as Group Financial Controller at Genuit Group plc. The Board has confirmed continuity arrangements during the transition period.
retail_take: Experienced CFO replacement with strong manufacturing sector track record suggests confidence in management continuity; smooth handover process reduces execution risk for investors.

headline: Annual Report 2026 and Notice of AGM
brief: Games Workshop publishes 2026 Annual Report and AGM notice; shareholder meeting scheduled for 16 September.
summary: Games Workshop has published its Annual Report and financial statements for the 52-week period ending 31 May 2026, along with Notice of the 2026 AGM and proxy forms. The AGM will be held at the company's Nottingham headquarters (1 Willow Road, NG7 2WS) at 10:00 a.m. on 16 September 2026. The documents have been uploaded to the FCA's National Storage Mechanism and are available on the company's investor relations website.
retail_take: Routine regulatory filing; standard AGM documentation and annual results disclosure. No material information disclosed in announcement itself; market focus will be on full report contents when reviewed.

headline: Banco Comercial Português, S.A. informs about Bank Millennium (Poland) results in H1 2026
Hussar Drill Mobilisation/Water Well drilling
brief: Water well drilling mobilised at Hussar EP513 ahead of Q3 2026 helium/hydrogen exploration well, fully funded by Harlequin partners.
summary: Georgina Energy's water well contractor has mobilised to the Hussar prospect (EP513) in Western Australia's Officer Basin. The Ensign 970 drill rig remains on schedule for Q3 2026 drilling, targeting the Townsend Formation and Neoproterozoic basement for helium, hydrogen and natural gas. The 50-day programme is fully funded by Harlequin and partners. Hussar holds IGR-certified prospective resources of 285 BCFG helium, 315 BCFG hydrogen, and 2.93 TCF natural gas, with potential in-situ value exceeding US$150 billion.
retail_take: Positive signal: project infrastructure advancing on schedule with third-party funding secured, reducing shareholder dilution risk and validating partner confidence in asset quality before drilling.

headline: Retail Offer
brief: Nativo Resources launches retail offer of up to £60k shares at 0.2p, alongside £640k institutional placing.
summary: Nativo Resources (LON: NTVO), a Peru-focused precious metals company, is conducting a retail offer of ordinary shares at 0.2p each to raise up to £60,000, open to UK existing shareholders via intermediaries from 28 July to 30 July 2026. The issue price represents a 4.8% discount to 27 July closing mid-market price. Simultaneously, the company is raising £640,000 through institutional placing and subscription. One warrant per two shares subscribed will be granted at 0.28p exercise price (40% premium), exercisable for 2.5 years. Admission expected 3 August 2026.
retail_take: Retail fundraising alongside larger institutional raise suggests capital needs but limited scale retail component may indicate weak demand or deliberate shareholder inclusion strategy; warrant sweeteners typical for smaller equity raises.

headline: Monthly Performance Update
brief: PIN reports 525.7p June NAV, +1.5% monthly. £2.1bn assets, 49% five-year return.
summary: Pantheon International's NAV per share reached 525.7p at 30 June 2026, up 7.8p (+1.5%) from May, driven by +5.6p FX gains and +4.6p from £63.9m share buybacks at 22% discount to NAV. Private equity assets stood at £2.184bn with £258m cash. The trust generated £209.6m net cash inflow including £204.8m from strategic portfolio sale. Five-year NAV total return reached 49%; one-year performance 6.8%. New commitments of £33.3m made to Nordic, Australian and US buyout funds.
retail_take: Steady monthly performance with positive FX tailwinds and value accretive buybacks at significant discounts supports the trust's long-term NAV growth narrative, though near-term returns remain modest.

headline: Dividend
brief: Games Workshop declares £1.40 per share dividend; 2026/27 total reaches £2.30 versus £1.40 prior year.
summary: Games Workshop declared a dividend of £1.40 per share on 28 July 2026, bringing total dividends announced for 2026/27 to £2.30, compared to £1.40 in 2025/26. Payment is scheduled for 5 October 2026 to shareholders registered on 28 August 2026, with ex-dividend date 27 August 2026. The increase aligns with the company's stated dividend policy.
retail_take: 64% increase in annual dividend signals strong cash generation and shareholder-friendly capital allocation, likely viewed positively by income-focused investors and the market.

headline: Half-year Financial Report
brief: Barclays Bank UK PLC publishes H1 2026 interim results on the FCA's National Storage Mechanism.
summary: Barclays Bank UK PLC announced its 2026 interim results on 28 July 2026, submitted to the FCA's National Storage Mechanism and available via the Barclays investor relations website. The announcement includes management presentations, financial tables, webcast replays, and Pillar 3 regulatory capital reports across multiple Barclays entities. Next scheduled results release is Q3 2026 on 22 October 2026.
retail_take: Routine regulatory filing of interim results; no specific financial figures disclosed in announcement itself, requiring access to linked documents for material content analysis and market impact assessment.

headline: Special Dividend
brief: TruFin confirms special dividend of £0.4303 per share, totalling £22.5m, following tender offer completion.
summary: TruFin plc has confirmed the special dividend value at £0.4303 per Ordinary Share, following completion of its Tender Offer announced 27 July 2026. The total aggregate return to shareholders is £22,513,707, payable 28 August 2026 to holders on register at 7 August 2026. Ex-dividend trading commences 6 August 2026.
retail_take: Capital return demonstrates shareholder-friendly capital allocation following tender completion; signals confidence in balance sheet, though tender context suggests prior share consolidation.

headline: Additional Listing Director/PDMR Shareholding
brief: Star Energy issues 55,800 SIP shares; two PDMRs acquire 6,102 shares each at 14.75p
summary: Star Energy Group PLC has applied to list 55,800 ordinary shares (0.002p each) on AIM under its Share Incentive Plan, expected to admit around 31 July 2026. Two PDMRs participated: CFO Frances Ward and CEO Ross Glover each acquired 6,102 shares at 14.75p on 24 July 2026 via matching allocation under the SIP. Post-issuance, total voting rights stand at 193,088,184 ordinary shares. The SIP is a tax-efficient employee scheme with 1-to-1 matching (potentially 2-to-1 upon production targets), subject to 3-year vesting.
retail_take: Routine disclosure of PDMR share acquisition through established employee incentive plan; insider purchases at consistent pricing signal management confidence but represent standard scheme participation rather than material new investment.

headline: Board Changes and Reconfirmation of FY26 Outlook
brief: CEO Chris Walters steps down; COO Chris Webster becomes Managing Director. Company cuts costs by £0.3m and reconfirms FY26 outlook amid delayed hydrogen rollout.
summary: Chris Walters (CEO since September 2018) departs 31 July 2026 by mutual agreement; Chris Webster (COO since April 2022) assumes Managing Director role and joins Board immediately. Sally Millen (Finance Director since November 2024) also joins Board. Richard Staveley (Non-Executive Director, Harwood Capital representative) steps down 30 September 2026. Board changes yield £0.3m annual central cost reduction with targeting of matching additional savings. FY26 reconfirms strong H2 performance, full-year revenue expected similar to FY25 (£16.6m, adjusted EBITDA £0.8m). FY27 forecasts modest defence-driven growth; hydrogen revenues prudently removed from forecasts.
retail_take: Leadership continuity concerns offset by internal promotion of experienced COO and cost discipline in response to hydrogen market disappointments. Market likely views cautiously given delayed hydrogen growth but positively notes focused defence strategy and operational improvements under Webster.

headline: Board Changes
brief: Restore PLC transitions leadership: CEO Charles Skinner becomes Chair; CFO Dan Baker promoted to CEO effective 1 January 2027.
summary: Charles Skinner, who returned as CEO in 2023 and delivered on financial targets, moves to Non-Executive Chair. Dan Baker, CFO since 2023, succeeds him as CEO following a thorough search process. Jamie Hopkins transitions from Non-Executive Chair to Senior Independent Director, replacing Patrick Butcher. Patrick remains as Non-Executive Director and Audit Committee Chair. The Board will identify a successor to Dan as CFO. Under Skinner's tenure, Restore achieved strong performance: FY2025 revenue £304.7m (2024: £240.0m), adjusted operating margin 20.8% (2024: 19.5%), and adjusted PBT £40.6m (2024: £33.2m).
retail_take: Orderly succession with internal promotion of proven CFO who helped drive strong financial performance suggests continuity and confidence; market likely views positively as Baker has demonstrated operational capability while Skinner remains as Chair to provide stability.

headline: PCA / PDMR Dealing
brief: DP Poland director-linked entity purchases 300,000 shares; Concert Party stake rises to 29.63%.
summary: AMC V Leonardo SARL, associated with Non-Executive Directors Przemysław Głębocki and Jakub Chechelski, purchased 300,000 ordinary shares at 6.99p on 27 July 2026. The Malaccan Holdings Ltd Concert Party now holds 279,725,426 shares representing 29.63% of issued capital. DP Poland operates 142 Domino's locations across Poland and Croatia, plus 70 Pizzeria 105 venues.
retail_take: Routine director-linked share purchase indicating continued insider confidence; stake increase to near-30% threshold is administrative in nature rather than signalling material strategic shift.

headline: Final Results, Notice of AGM & Dividend
brief: Samuel Heath reports flat revenue and halved profits amid tariffs, restructuring costs and market headwinds; maintains dividend.
summary: Samuel Heath & Sons PLC posted FY2026 revenue of £14.826m (flat vs £14.769m prior year) with profit before tax down 68% to £375k from £1.163m, hit by US tariffs (£384k), UK tax changes affecting international clients, and £383k restructuring costs. Gross profit fell to £6.577m from £6.839m. Cash improved to £2.802m; net assets rose to £12.973m. Directors recommend maintaining final dividend at 8.5625p per share (total declared £331k). AGM scheduled 3 September 2026.
retail_take: Profits halved due to external headwinds (tariffs, tax policy), not operational failure; management restructured; dividend maintained signals confidence but Q1 shows improvement tempered by expected summer weakness and order decline. Mixed signal.

headline: Warrant Extension, Director Shareholding & RPT
brief: Mendell Helium extends warrant exercise periods to December 2026; CEO and Chairman hold affected warrants.
summary: Mendell Helium extended exercise periods for 25,955,553 warrants expiring 26 December 2026. The 4p 2025 Warrants (10.6m outstanding) now have mandatory exercise if share price exceeds 7p for ten trading days. CEO Nick Tulloch holds 1.7m 6p 2024 Warrants and Chairman Eric Boyle holds 416,666; both recused from board decisions. Independent directors confirmed transaction terms fair. Company has 108.5m warrants outstanding representing potential dilution.
retail_take: Warrant extension is administrative but signals management expects shares won't reach exercise prices organically; mandatory exercise clause at 7p indicates confidence in near-term performance. Director holdings create potential conflicts but were independently approved.

headline: Appointment of Executive Chairman
brief: Helge Weiner-Trapness appointed Executive Chairman, replacing Peter Jensen after 15+ years. Transition supports Hong Kong dual listing strategy.
summary: Helge Weiner-Trapness, Chief Strategy Officer since January 2026, becomes Executive Chairman succeeding Peter Jensen OBE who steps down after 15 years on the board and 11 years as Chairman. Weiner-Trapness brings 30+ years investment banking experience, including Vice Chairman at HSBC, and serves on the Gavi vaccine funding board. Jensen remains as Non-Executive Director during transition, departing at next AGM. The appointment positions leadership to support the company's pursuit of a potential dual primary listing on Hong Kong Stock Exchange alongside its AIM listing, targeting Asian market expansion and R&D development.
retail_take: Leadership change with strategic credentials for Hong Kong expansion is moderately positive, though market may monitor execution risk; Jensen's long tenure ending could raise governance questions despite smooth transition plans.

headline: Former Endesa Chief Executive Joins Berkeley Board
brief: José Bogas Gálvez, former Endesa CEO with 40+ years energy sector experience, appointed Non-Executive Director.
summary: Berkeley Energia appoints José Bogas Gálvez as independent Non-Executive Director effective 28 July 2026. Bogas spent 12 years as CEO of Spanish utility Endesa and brings 40+ years experience in Spanish and European energy sectors. Compensation: A$45,000 annual director fee, A$15,000 committee fee, plus 2m unlisted options at A$0.80 vesting over 18 months. Appointment intended to strengthen Berkeley's influence in Spain and assist with resolving permitting for the Salamanca Project.
retail_take: Positive signal: Bogas's high-profile appointment and Spanish government connections suggest Berkeley is advancing its flagship Salamanca uranium project and gaining credibility for permitting negotiations.

headline: Notice of Q2 and H1 2026 Financial Results
brief: Atalaya Mining to report Q2 and H1 2026 results on 11 August with analyst webcast and investor presentation.
summary: Atalaya Mining (LSE: ATYM), a European copper producer operating the Proyecto Riotinto complex in southwest Spain, will release unaudited Q2 and H1 2026 financial results on Tuesday, 11 August 2026. CEO Alberto Lavandeira and CFO César Sánchez will host a webcast at 09:00 BST and an Investor Meet Company presentation at 11:00 BST. The company operates the Cerro Colorado open pit mine and 15 Mtpa processing plant, with growth projects including Proyecto Masa Valverde, Riotinto East, and an 80% earn-in on Proyecto Touro.
retail_take: Routine earnings announcement with no material new information disclosed; market reaction will depend on actual results and guidance provided on 11 August.

headline: Notice of Annual General Meeting and Annual Report
brief: Yellow Cake announces 2026 AGM scheduled for 8 September; publishes annual report and proxy materials.
summary: Yellow Cake PLC, a uranium sector specialist holding 23.21 million pounds of U₃O₈ in storage across Canada and France, has published its 2026 Annual Report and AGM Notice. The AGM will be held on 8 September 2026 at 10:00am in Jersey. The company holds a ten-year Framework Agreement with Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer, differentiating it from peers. Shareholders will receive hard copy or electronic notification of AGM materials depending on their communication preferences.
retail_take: Routine regulatory filing and governance disclosure; AGM announcement is procedural. Material focus should be on annual results contained within the published report rather than this notice itself.

headline: Notice of Results
brief: Caledonia Mining to publish Q2 2026 results August 10, followed by investor presentation.
summary: Caledonia Mining Corporation Plc will release operating and financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 on Monday, August 10, 2026. A remote investor presentation and analyst call will follow at 2:00pm London time. The company is a Zimbabwe-focused gold producer with 64% stake in Blanket Mine, targeting 75-80,000 oz annual production, plus development projects including Bilboes Sulphide and Motapa/Maligreen claims.
retail_take: Routine results announcement with standard investor call; no material news disclosed pre-release, so market will await August 10 for operational and financial metrics to assess production, cash generation, and project progress.

headline: Notice of Results and Investor Presentation
brief: Concurrent Technologies to announce interim H1 2025 results on 7 September with analyst and investor presentations scheduled.
summary: Concurrent Technologies PLC will release interim results for the six months ended 30 June 2025 on Monday, 7 September 2026. CEO Miles Adcock and CFO Kim Garrod will host an in-person analyst briefing at 9am at Investec's London offices. A separate retail investor presentation will be held on 11 September 2026 at 12pm via the Investor Meet Company platform, with pre-event question submission available.
retail_take: Routine regulatory notice announcing results timing and presentation arrangements; no material information disclosed; standard investor engagement activity.

headline: First Sale Under Helium Offtake Agreement
brief: Helium One's 50% Colorado asset achieves first offtake agreement sale; production ramping toward design capacity.
summary: Blue Star Helium (operator of Galactica-Pegasus in Colorado) delivered its second helium trailer on 28 July 2026, representing the first sale under a short-term offtake agreement. The Pinon Canyon plant has stabilised at current production levels with regular scheduled trailer exchanges now underway. The joint venture plans three new development wells in H2 2026 and potential deepening of existing wells to increase output toward full design capacity. Helium One holds 50% equity in the project.
retail_take: Transition from exploration to revenue-generating operations with concrete sales activity de-risks Helium One's US asset; demonstrates production stability and near-term cash flow prospects, likely viewed positively by growth-stage exploration investors.

headline: Update on logistics disruption and vessel incident
brief: Ferrexpo vessel struck by Russian drones in Black Sea; crew member killed, cargo at risk, liquidity critical until end-August.
summary: A Ferrexpo vessel carrying 55,000 tonnes of high-grade DR-grade pellets was damaged by Russian drone strikes in Ukrainian Black Sea waters; one crew member died in the incident. The company has ~189,000 tonnes designated for shipment worth ~$20 million in production costs. Following vessel cancellations by shipowners, the Group expects Black Sea export route unavailable foreseeable future, creating material liquidity impact. Cash runway now forecast to end-August 2026 only. Company pursuing urgent $100 million+ equity fundraise to support working capital.
retail_take: Severe near-term liquidity crisis with geopolitical headwinds and fundraising uncertainty likely triggers significant market sell-off; survival depends on capital raise completion within weeks.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: M.P. Evans repurchased and cancelled 2,941 shares at an average price of 1,694.29p on 27 July 2026.
summary: M.P. Evans Group PLC purchased 2,941 of its own shares for cancellation on 27 July 2026 via broker Cavendish Capital Markets. Shares traded between 1,684.00p and 1,700.00p, with a volume-weighted average price of 1,694.29p. Following cancellation, the company has 52,151,337 shares in issue, representing total voting rights.
retail_take: Routine share buyback reducing share count; typically signals management confidence in valuation but represents non-material capital allocation against current share price levels.

headline: Kumba Iron Ore interim results 2026
brief: Kumba Iron Ore reports H1 2026 interim results with strong operational performance and cash generation.
summary: Kumba Iron Ore delivered H1 2026 results with an average realised export price of US$90/wmt (8% above benchmark), C1 unit cost of US$46/wmt, and 35% EBITDA margin. The company generated R1.9 billion attributable free cash flow, closed with R12.1 billion net cash, and declared an interim dividend of R7.90 per share. Operations achieved fatality-free records exceeding 10 years at Sishen and 3+ years at Kolomela, while women comprise 32% of the workforce.
retail_take: Strong pricing relative to costs, robust cash generation, and disciplined capital allocation likely viewed positively by markets, though elevated C1 costs from external headwinds warrant monitoring.

headline: New Website
brief: Marechale Capital PLC launches modernised corporate website reflecting its evolution as UK's first quoted fully integrated digital merchant bank.
summary: Marechale Capital plc (AIM: MAC) announced the launch of its new corporate website at marechalecapital.com on 28 July 2026. The site reflects the group's transformation across four operating businesses—Marechale Capital, Stanford Capital Partners, Blubird Global, and NJC Capital Management—offering integrated services in corporate finance, capital markets, tokenisation, and asset management. The platform is underpinned by ownership of the Blubird technology platform. CEO Patrick Booth-Clibborn stated the website better communicates the group's strategy as a bridge between traditional and digital finance, with investor relations and AIM Rule 26 disclosures now centrally available.
retail_take: Corporate website refresh is a routine operational communication with no material business impact. Market will likely treat this as non-event—purely cosmetic rebranding exercise reflecting existing strategic positioning rather than new developments.

headline: Strategic Rationale of UAE Expansion
brief: AEG outlines strategic rationale for UAE expansion focusing on AI infrastructure, energy and water security ahead of AGM.
summary: Active Energy Group explained its UAE expansion strategy ahead of its 30 July 2026 AGM, positioning itself at the convergence of AI infrastructure, reliable power, and water management. The company argues AI datacentres require integrated solutions delivering both energy and water resources. UAE's government investment in digital infrastructure, desalination, and regional priorities around energy, water, food security and supply chain resilience align with AEG's objectives. Management believes this integrated infrastructure platform will generate long-term shareholder value while positioning AEG within sectors expected to receive sustained investment over the coming decade.
retail_take: Non-regulatory announcement providing strategic context rather than material news; positions AEG in high-growth sectors (AI, infrastructure) but lacks concrete project details or financial metrics, likely neutral to marginally positive for growth-focused investors.

headline: First commercial agreement for EpiSwitch® Orion
brief: Oxford BioDynamics signs first commercial agreement for EpiSwitch Orion platform with UK government-funded psoriatic arthritis research programme.
summary: Oxford BioDynamics has secured its first paid commercial agreement for EpiSwitch Orion, a cloud-based 3D genomics platform, as part of the OPTIMISE programme—a UK Department of Health and Social Care-funded translational research initiative. The agreement involves collaboration between NDORMS (University of Oxford), University of Glasgow, King's College London, and Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust. OBD will receive payment for biomarker discovery work and genomic sequence processing using EpiSwitch Orion on approximately 240 whole-genome sequenced patient samples with psoriatic arthritis, developing predictive classifiers for biologic therapy response. Financial terms remain undisclosed.
retail_take: First commercial validation of Orion platform demonstrates real-world adoption and market demand; signals potential for significant revenue generation given CEO's estimate of 15,000 genomics PIs as addressable market, though undisclosed terms limit impact assessment.

headline: Portfolio news: Pulsiv agreement with Delta Matrix
brief: Pulsiv's energy-efficient power conversion technology secures exclusive manufacturing deal with Delta Matrix, enabling first commercial USB modules.
summary: Pulsiv Limited has appointed Delta Matrix Limited as exclusive manufacturer and wholesaler for USB modules based on its OSMIUM AC-to-DC power conversion technology. The Easby Group subsidiary will produce and distribute modules for applications including power chargers and building/vehicle-integrated sockets. With over 2 billion wall sockets sold globally annually and USB products expected to account for 600 million yearly installations, demand is driven by new UK/EU energy efficiency regulations. Pulsiv's technology offers superior efficiency, reduced heat waste, smaller designs, and improved reliability. Frontier IP Group holds 17.3% equity in Pulsiv. The technology has won PSMA awards and is protected by 95+ patents.
retail_take: Positive signal: tangible commercialisation milestone for portfolio company with substantial market opportunity (2bn+ addressable units) and regulatory tailwinds, though near-term revenue impact uncertain for Frontier IP.

headline: Notice of AGM
brief: Revolution Beauty Group announces 2026 AGM scheduled for 13 August 2026 at London offices.
summary: Revolution Beauty Group PLC (AIM: REVB) has scheduled its 2026 Annual General Meeting for 10:00 a.m. on Thursday 13 August 2026 at Strand Hanson's offices in London. The company published audited FY26 results on 22 July 2026, with Notice of AGM and Annual Report dispatched to shareholders. The global mass beauty retailer operates ~17,500 retail doors across UK, USA and international markets, employs 229 people, and operates multi-brand, multi-category DTC and wholesale operations.
retail_take: Routine corporate governance disclosure; the AGM scheduling and results publication are standard procedural announcements with no material business implications signaled in the notice itself.

headline: Doc re. ASA subscription investment
brief: Beacon Rise raises £50k via advanced subscription agreement; total ASA funds reach £700k pending completion.
summary: Beacon Rise Holdings has entered an advanced subscription agreement (ASA) with a new investor to raise approximately £50,000 gross proceeds, bringing total ASA funds raised to £700,000 pending completion. Net proceeds will fund transaction fees for proposed acquisitions and admission, plus working capital. ASA subscribers will receive ordinary shares at the price of any concurrent equity fundraise, or £1.80 per share if admission hasn't occurred by 28 August 2026.
retail_take: Continued fundraising ahead of proposed acquisitions and listing suggests execution progress, though reliance on conditional ASAs and tight admission deadline indicates some execution risk remains.

headline: Admission to AIM and First Day of Dealings
Talking Medicines CLN & Distribution Commitment
brief: Tern invests £117k in Talking Medicines CLNs; raises shareholder distribution commitment to 70%.
summary: Tern PLC invested £117,195 in convertible loan notes issued by Talking Medicines, receiving uplifted principal value of £234,389 at 10% interest, convertible at 20% discount on exit or £2m+ fundraising, maturing November 2029. Tern maintains 23.8% equity stake while increasing CLN holding to £1.02m. Board enhanced shareholder distribution commitment from 50% to 70% of net proceeds from individual portfolio exits exceeding £1m, reflecting confidence in portfolio maturity and transaction prospects.
retail_take: Positive signal: increased distribution commitment suggests confidence in near-term exit opportunities, while attractive CLN terms demonstrate management's capital discipline and shareholder alignment focus.

headline: Half-year Financial Report
brief: Barclays submits H1 2026 interim results to FCA National Storage Mechanism on 28 July 2026.
summary: Barclays Bank PLC announced its 2026 interim results on 28 July 2026, filing full unedited text to the FCA's National Storage Mechanism. Supporting documents include results announcement, presentation slides, financial tables, management speech, Q&A transcript, webcast replay, and Pillar 3 regulatory capital reports. Q3 2026 results are scheduled for 22 October 2026.
retail_take: Routine regulatory filing of half-year results; no material details disclosed in announcement itself—investors must review linked documents for earnings, capital ratios, and strategic updates to assess performance.

headline: Notice of Annual General Meeting
brief: Powerhouse Energy Group announces AGM scheduled for 3 September 2026 in London.
summary: Powerhouse Energy Group plc (AIM: PHE) has set its Annual General Meeting for 2:00 p.m. on 3 September 2026 at the Garraway Room, 1 Cornhill, London EC3V 3ND. The Notice of AGM will be posted to shareholders, with proxy voting forms due by 1 September 2026 at 2:00 p.m. (48 hours before the meeting). Shareholders may vote via CREST, postal form, or email to the company's registrars Neville Registrars Limited.
retail_take: Routine disclosure; no read-through. Standard AGM notification with procedural voting information; no material business announcements or substantive corporate developments indicated.

headline: Issue of Equity, Total Voting Rights
brief: Red Rock Resources issues 95.2m shares to settle £20k loan; total voting rights now 9.68bn.
summary: Red Rock Resources plc issued 95,238,095 ordinary shares of £0.0001 each to settle a £20,000 loan. The shares are being admitted to AIM trading on or around 3 August 2026. Following the issue, the company's total issued ordinary share capital comprises 9,675,142,514 shares, representing the total voting rights in the company. All shares carry equal voting rights and none are held in treasury.
retail_take: Routine disclosure of share issuance for debt settlement and voting rights notification. Modest capital raise relative to existing share base; minimal immediate market impact expected.

headline: Network Partnerships with Google and ByteDance
brief: Potentially AI secures Google and ByteDance partnerships with $350k cloud credits and discounted model access.
summary: Potentially AI has been accepted into Google for Startups Cloud Program's AI tier, receiving up to US$350,000 in Google Cloud credits over two years plus access to Vertex AI and Gemini models. The company also joined BytePlus Partner Network, gaining discounted access to ByteDance's AI models including its Seed family and early access to new releases. Both partnerships provide technical support and training. The consumer app nears rollout with a waiting list available.
retail_take: Positive signal for pre-revenue AI startup: partnerships with major tech firms validate business model, extend cash runway, and provide competitive infrastructure advantages as it scales toward H2 2026 product launches.

headline: ACCRUFeR® Phase 3 pediatric trial published
brief: Shield Therapeutics' ACCRUFeR® pediatric trial published, showing safety and effectiveness in children from 2 months old.
summary: The FORTIS Phase 3 trial comparing ferric maltol to ferrous sulfate in children aged 1 month-17 years showed clinically significant hemoglobin improvements across all groups (P<0.0001). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 6.5% of ferric maltol patients versus 13% of ferrous sulfate patients; zero discontinuations due to adverse events in the ferric maltol arm versus one in the comparator. The liquid formulation registration is planned to support treatment of children aged 2 and above, expanding the product's approved pediatric use beyond the current 10+ years (US) and 12+ years (EU).
retail_take: Positive catalyst: publication validates ferric maltol's pediatric safety and superior tolerability profile, supporting market expansion into younger age groups and strengthening competitive positioning in the $2.3B iron deficiency market.

headline: FY26 Trading Update
brief: Dotdigital delivers FY26 in line with expectations; ARR growth accelerates to 18% with AI platform expansion.
summary: Dotdigital reported FY26 revenue of £90.9m (up 8%), with core CXDP recurring revenue reaching £76.8m (up 14% to 84% of total revenue). Forward-looking contracted ARR grew 18% to £85.4m (8% organically), improving from 6% at half-year. Cash fell to £17.1m from £36.2m due to US$30m Alia acquisition (4 months contributed £10.0m ARR). Social Snowball delivered 33% ARR growth. Profit and margins in line with consensus; new AI products (Agents, MCP server, Loyalty platform) launched post-year-end.
retail_take: Results meet expectations with improving organic momentum and successful acquisitions, but cash depletion and flat organic total revenue (ex-acquisitions) may temper enthusiasm; medium-term growth positioning looks solid.

headline: Company Update
brief: Rift Helium advancing Tanzania helium project; EIA completion expected Q3 2026, 3D seismic planned thereafter.
summary: Rift Helium (AIM: RIFT) reports progress on its Upepo Project in Tanzania's Rukwa Basin. Environmental Impact Assessment in final stages with completion expected Q3 2026. 3D seismic acquisition planned Q3 2026 post-EIA approval, with updated independent resource assessment targeted Q1 2027. Company fully funded for seismic programme and two-well exploration drilling (first well H1 2027). CPR identifies P50 prospective resources of ~19 Bcf helium and mean estimate ~41 Bcf. Site conditions favourable; no material long-lead items identified to delay mobilisation.
retail_take: On-track execution in early-stage exploration with clear milestones through 2027; positive progression but drilling results remain years away, maintaining high execution risk typical of early-stage explorers.

headline: Half-Year Trading Update and Notice of Results
brief: Uniphar posts 11% adjusted EPS growth in H1 2026 with 7% organic gross profit growth across divisions, on track for full-year targets.
summary: Uniphar delivered approximately 11% adjusted EPS growth in H1 2026 driven by 7% organic gross profit growth. Uniphar Pharma achieved high single-digit growth targeting double-digit full-year growth; Medtech and Supply Chain & Retail both delivered high and mid-single-digit growth respectively. Net Bank Debt/EBITDA stands at 2.4x. The new Irish distribution facility launch is deferred to February 2027 with €20m incremental capex, providing FY2026 adjusted EPS benefit. The group targets €200m EBITDA by 2028 with 80%+ organic growth, maintaining strong liquidity and an active M&A pipeline.
retail_take: Solid operational progress with in-line guidance delivery and strategic capex timing adjustment that benefits near-term EPS. Likely read as positive given consistent growth across divisions and confidence in medium-term targets.

headline: Six months ended 30 June 2026
brief: Forterra reports resilient H1 2026 performance amid challenging markets; maintains full-year guidance despite geopolitical headwinds.
summary: Building products manufacturer Forterra delivered H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of £27.0m (down 9.7% YoY) with revenue of £168.8m (down 13.5%), but improved EBITDA margin to 16.0% from 15.3%. Like-for-like revenue declined 9.3% as UK brick industry despatches fell 8%, though Forterra outperformed the market. Management implemented £2m annual cost savings through restructuring and production alignment. Net debt stands at £74.5m (1.5x adjusted EBITDA). Interim dividend held at 1.7p. Board expects H2 demand similar to H1, supporting full-year consensus expectations of £55.6m adjusted EBITDA, with confidence in recovery-driven tailwinds from recent capacity investments.
retail_take: Guidance maintenance despite weaker H1 and macro uncertainty is stabilising but modest; margin expansion and market outperformance suggest operational discipline, though challenging demand outlook limits near-term upside.

headline: H1 2026 Trading Update
brief: Portmeirion H1 2026 sales flat at £36.4m; tableware up 4.1% with strong US growth offsetting UK and Korea weakness.
summary: Portmeirion Group reported H1 2026 sales of £36.4m, flat year-on-year at constant currency, with tableware growing 4.1%. North America surged 13.6% (US +17%), while UK declined 14.4% and South Korea fell 15.7% due to strategic resets. Net debt improved significantly to £6.2m from £17.5m following an £18.6m equity raise and £3m US tariff claim recovery. The group completed senior leadership appointments and maintained full-year guidance for 3-5% revenue growth and lower adjusted losses than FY25.
retail_take: Market likely views this positively: turnaround strategy delivering despite H1 challenges, balance sheet transformation, strong US momentum, and clear operational progress against 2026 objectives; however, UK market weakness and Wax Lyrical disposal signal ongoing portfolio repositioning.

headline: Half-year Results
brief: Inchcape reports H1 2026 results with 9% volume growth; increases share buyback to £250m; guides for >10% FY2026 EPS growth.
summary: Inchcape PLC posted H1 2026 revenue of £4.7bn (+9% reported, +7% constant currency), with organic growth of 5% driven by distribution contract wins. Adjusted operating profit fell 2% in constant currency to £248m, with margins down 40bps to 5.3%, weighed by APAC headwinds offset by Americas and Europe & Africa strength. Adjusted PBT declined 6% to £188m; adjusted basic EPS flat at 35.5p. Free cash flow reached £84m; net leverage 0.5x. The company increased its share buyback programme by £75m to £250m and raised interim dividend 14% to 10.8p, forecasting full-year adjusted EPS growth exceeding 10% with H2-weighted performance.
retail_take: Strong volume growth and margin expansion in Americas/Europe offset APAC weakness; increased buyback signals confidence in cash generation and balance sheet strength, supporting shareholder returns guidance. Market likely views this as solid execution on strategy with improving capital allocation, though second-half weighting creates near-term uncertainty.

headline: Acquisition of Plus Group
brief: Tavistock acquires 87.9% of Plus Group for £900k upfront plus £3.6m over 18 months, with up to £11.5m deferred consideration, to accelerate AI capabilities.
summary: Tavistock Investments PLC is acquiring 87.9% of Plus Group, a provider of AI Agent technology and paraplanning services, for £900,000 cash upfront and £3.6 million over 18 months, with potential deferred consideration of up to £11.5 million over four years based on performance. Plus Group generated £998,000 turnover and £340,000 EBITDA in the year to 30 September 2025. The acquisition supports Tavistock's rebranding to Vertex Group and strategic pivot toward AI-enabled advisory tools that enhance adviser productivity rather than replace human advisers, building on recent acquisitions of Alpha Beta Partners and Lifetime Financial Management.
retail_take: Market likely views this positively as a bolt-on acquisition supporting Tavistock's technology-enabled advisory strategy and rebranding narrative, though modest absolute scale and heavy earn-out structure (£11.5m of £15.4m total) suggest manageable downside risk.

headline: Operational and Corporate Update
brief: Premier African Minerals delays July restart of Zulu lithium plant pending Long Stop Date extension negotiations with Canmax.
summary: Premier African Minerals has postponed plant operations at its Zulu Lithium and Tantalum Project beyond July 2026 while negotiating a Long Stop Date extension under existing prepayment and offtake arrangements with Canmax Technologies. The company is implementing plant upgrades and building ore inventory on the ROM pad. Canmax is reviewing operational data from the upgraded flotation circuit. No guarantee of extension agreement exists, with revised operating timetable to be confirmed upon conclusion of discussions. The extension and next production campaign are intended to demonstrate sustained performance for ongoing strategic investor engagement.
retail_take: Delay signals operational uncertainty and dependence on third-party approval, though constructive negotiations and plant optimisation efforts are positive. Market likely to view extension uncertainty negatively until formal agreement reached.

headline: GreenTech Metals Quarterly Activities Report
brief: GreenTech Metals (30% owned by Alien) advances Munni Munni PGE-copper project with Phase 1 drilling results and major resource re-estimation underway.
summary: GreenTech completed Phase 1 drilling at Munni Munni PGE-Cu-Ni Project in Western Australia, validating historical data and identifying thicker mineralised zones with grades up to 8.8g/t PGE3. An independent geochemical review identified a 5km x 2km copper anomaly and high-priority basal targets. GreenTech secured A$7.5m funding, appointed Chief Geologist Rachel Backus and Technical Advisor Heida Mani, and will conduct 4,750m RC and 3,560m diamond drilling plus co-funded EM surveys starting August 2026. Alien holds 30% free carried to feasibility study completion and 37.9m GreenTech shares (10% stake).
retail_take: Positive catalyst for Alien: exploration upside validation, major drilling campaign commencing, new technical appointments signal acceleration, though outcomes remain exploratory and carry execution risk.

headline: 2026 First Half Results
brief: Unilever posts strong H1 2026 with 4.8% underlying sales growth, led by volume gains. Upgrades full-year guidance.
summary: Unilever delivered 4.8% underlying sales growth in H1 2026 (4.2% volume, 0.6% price), accelerating to 5.8% USG in Q2—the best volume quarter in over a decade. Power Brands grew 6.0%, driving performance across Beauty & Wellbeing (5.9%), Personal Care (4.8%), and Home Care (7.6%). Underlying operating margin improved 10bps to 20.3%. The company completed its €800m productivity programme ahead of schedule and finished a €1.5bn share buyback. Unilever Foods separation from McCormick proceeds on track for mid-2027 completion, with London secondary listing announced 23 July. Full-year outlook upgraded to 4-6% underlying sales growth with ~3% volume growth.
retail_take: Strong volume-led growth, margin expansion, and successful execution signal operational momentum despite macro uncertainty. Foods separation unlocks HPC purity while raising investor clarity, likely supporting re-rating.

headline: Results for the 52 week period ended 31 May 2026
brief: Games Workshop reports record revenue and profit for FY2026, with core business growth offsetting licensing decline.
summary: Games Workshop posted record revenue of £659.7m (FY2025: £617.5m) and profit before tax of £275.7m (FY2025: £262.8m) for the 52 weeks ended 31 May 2026. Core revenue grew to £626.8m from £565.0m, while licensing revenue declined to £32.9m from £52.5m. Core operating profit reached £245.1m versus £211.8m prior year. Earnings per share increased to 624.0p from 594.9p. Dividends declared and paid were 485p per share (FY2025: 520p). Cash generation improved with net cash increase of £210.3m pre-dividends.
retail_take: Strong core business momentum and record profits likely appeal to investors, though licensing revenue decline and lower dividend per share may temper enthusiasm slightly. Operational gearing visible in margin expansion suggests pricing power.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: AEP Plantations repurchased 55,248 shares at 173-181p as part of ongoing buyback programme.
summary: AEP Plantations purchased 55,248 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 via Cavendish Capital Markets at prices between 173p and 181p (VWAP 178.56p), held in treasury. Since the buyback programme's 6 July announcement, the company has repurchased 748,216 shares total. Post-purchase, AEP has 399,762,720 shares in issue with 16,917,456 held in treasury, leaving 382,845,264 voting shares outstanding.
retail_take: Routine share buyback execution within announced programme; modest daily tranche suggests orderly execution. No strategic signal; mechanical capital management with modest accretive potential if shares held rather than cancelled.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: Hollywood Bowl Group repurchased 18,951 shares at 284.5-285p on 22-23 July for cancellation.
summary: Hollywood Bowl Group plc purchased 18,951 ordinary shares through Berenberg on 22-23 July 2026. On 22 July, 967 shares were bought at 284.5p; on 23 July, 17,984 shares were purchased at 285.0p. The shares will be cancelled. Total investment approximately £54,000 based on weighted average prices.
retail_take: Share buyback signals management confidence in valuation but modest scale suggests routine capital management rather than aggressive value creation signal.

headline: HUGO BOSS offer condition satisfied
brief: Frasers Group secures EU merger clearance for €38/share HUGO BOSS takeover; offer now unconditional.
summary: Frasers Group announced on 28 July 2026 that European Commission merger control clearance for its voluntary public takeover offer for HUGO BOSS AG has been granted, satisfying the final offer condition. The offer of €38.00 per HUGO BOSS share is now unconditional, with an additional acceptance period running until 13 August 2026. The takeover was first announced on 10 June 2026 with the offer document published 25 June 2026.
retail_take: Regulatory hurdle cleared removes last material risk to deal completion; signals transaction progressing on track toward closure with limited downside for shareholders accepting the offer.

headline: Interim Results for Six Months Ended 30 June 2026
brief: Unite Group reports H1 2026 results with adjusted EPS down 8% to 27.1p; plans major portfolio restructuring focused on top universities.
summary: Adjusted earnings fell 2% to £142m (H1 2025: £144.2m) and adjusted EPS declined 8% to 27.1p, reflecting higher interest costs and Empiric acquisition impacts. IFRS loss of £417.7m driven by 6.4% property valuation decline as yields rose. Company plans to dispose of 15,000-20,000 beds across 9 cities, reducing portfolio from 72,000 to 55,000-60,000 beds by reinvesting in top-tier universities. Net debt/EBITDA increased to 7.5x; EPRA NTA fell 9% to 865p. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance maintained at 41.5-43.0p.
retail_take: Market likely negative; property valuation declines, rising leverage, and earnings downgrades offset by strategic clarity and disposal activity. Portfolio restructuring is positive long-term but creates near-term uncertainty and balance sheet pressure.

headline: Publication of 2026 FY Annual Audited Report
brief: Zenith Energy publishes FY2026 results; CAD$28.3m loss driven by Tunisia arbitration costs and asset impairments.
summary: Zenith Energy reported a CAD$28.3m loss for FY2026 (vs CAD$1.1m profit in FY2025), primarily due to CAD$8.0m in arbitration costs against Tunisia, CAD$6.8m in asset impairments, CAD$1.7m Stockholm listing costs, and CAD$1.4m non-cash stock option charges. Revenues grew modestly to CAD$2.3m. The ICSID arbitration hearing concluded in April 2026; claims total ~US$700m across ICSID (US$572.65m) and ICC-2 (US$130m) proceedings. Italian renewable solar portfolio expanded to 193.5 MWp post-year-end; uranium exploration permits submitted in Italy. Post-period, Reveille Resources spun out as dedicated uranium vehicle; potential Daybreak Oil acquisition discussions commenced.
retail_take: Market likely views this negatively despite underlying operational stability—large extraordinary charges, Tunisia litigation uncertainty, and heavy reliance on speculative arbitration proceeds (~US$700m) create valuation difficulty. Positive spinoff of Reveille and solar expansion don't offset litigation risk.

headline: Placing and Subscription to Raise £640,000
brief: Nativo Resources raises £640k via placing and subscription at 0.2p per share, with additional up-to-£60k retail offer.
summary: Nativo Resources (LON: NTVO), a Peru-focused gold mining company, raised £640,000 gross through a placing of 210m shares and subscription of 110m shares at 0.2p each—a 4.8% discount to prior close. Additional retail offer of up to £60,000 available to eligible UK shareholders. Investors receive one warrant per two shares (0.28p exercise price, 2.5-year term). Net proceeds fund Gold Ore Processing Plant commissioning, Tesoro Gold development, tailings projects, and working capital. Directors Stephen Birrell (CEO) and Christian Yates (Chair) each subscribed 6.625m shares at 0.2p, satisfying £13,250 outstanding sums each. Admission expected 3 August 2026.
retail_take: Dilutive capital raise at a discount signals funding pressure, though proceeds targeting near-term catalysts (plant financing, offtake deals, Q4 2026 production) may appeal to growth investors. Warrant sweetener and director participation show confidence, but equity dilution and execution risk on production timeline merit caution.

headline: Trading Statement
brief: Kistos reports H1 2026 pro forma production of 20,500 boepd with $205m EBITDA and $259m cash. Maintains FY26 guidance.
summary: Independent energy company Kistos delivered H1 2026 pro forma production of 20,500 boepd against FY26 guidance of 19,000-21,000 boepd. Pro forma EBITDA reached ~$205m on realised prices of $104/bbl oil and 97p/therm gas. Cash position strengthened to $259m versus $179m at year-end 2025, with adjusted net debt at just $23m. 2P reserves reached 47.6 MMboe post-Balder Next project sanction; 2C resources estimated at 52.4 MMboe. Oman acquisition (Blocks 3&4, Block 9) nearing completion with Ministerial Approval obtained.
retail_take: Solid operational delivery with strong cash generation and low leverage supports growth trajectory, though market may focus on Oman completion timing and whether M&A pipeline justifies premium valuation.

headline: 2026 Half-year Financial Report
brief: Canal+ reports strong H1 2026 results with 40% revenue growth and 68% adjusted EBIT increase, driven by MultiChoice consolidation.
summary: Canal+ delivered H1 2026 revenue of €4,287m (up 40% YoY) and adjusted EBIT of €433m (up 68%), with organic growth excluding MultiChoice of 1.4% and 13% respectively. Free cash flow reached €414m. MultiChoice turnaround is underway with subscriber acquisition up 40%, and the group achieved €120m of its €250m full-year synergy target. Full-year 2026 guidance confirmed: flat revenue, €735m adjusted EBIT, and FCF above €250m. STUDIOCANAL performed strongly with major content acquisitions including Paddington 4 and extended UEFA rights across multiple European markets.
retail_take: Strong execution on MultiChoice integration with synergy delivery on track and robust cash generation supports guidance confidence, though H1 benefited from significant seasonality effects that may not repeat in H2.

headline: Strategic and business update
brief: Supply@ME expands SFE acquisition scope to include Italian credit intermediation business and working capital funding capabilities.
summary: Supply@ME is broadening its proposed acquisition from SFE beyond the original inventory ownership business to include an Italian regulated credit intermediation business (OAM-supervised) and inventory monetisation funding know-how. Negotiations continue on corporate and transaction-level funding with SFE Equity Investments SARL. Definitive documentation remains unsigned. The company is pursuing two potential Italian IM transactions: EUR 25 million with existing client Tekne S.p.A and another undisclosed opportunity. 2025 Annual Report and Accounts remain unpublished beyond the 30 April deadline.
retail_take: Expansion signals ambition but adds execution risk; acquisition remains non-binding and undefined, auditor delays and related-party concerns (CEO Zamboni's indirect SFE interest) raise governance questions; material uncertainty remains.

headline: Issue of Equity and TVR
brief: Rockwood Strategic issues 100,000 shares at 317.66p per share via blocklisting facility.
summary: Rockwood Strategic PLC issued 100,000 ordinary shares of 5 pence each at 317.66 pence per share on 27 July 2026 from its blocklisting facility for cash settlement on 29 July 2026. Post-issuance, the Company will have 61,003,760 ordinary shares in issue with no treasury holdings. This establishes the voting rights denominator for FCA Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules compliance calculations.
retail_take: Routine capital raise via existing facility; modest equity dilution. Market likely views this as administrative financing activity with limited read-through unless context suggests strategic need.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: IHG repurchases 1,000 shares at average $158.76 for cancellation under existing authority.
summary: InterContinental Hotels Group purchased 1,000 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 through Goldman Sachs International on the London Stock Exchange at prices ranging from $157.85 to $159.95, with a volume-weighted average of $158.7617. The shares will be cancelled. Following this transaction, IHG has 148,604,282 shares in issue, excluding 5,431,782 held in treasury. This continues the buyback programme authorized at the May 2025 AGM and announced on 17 February 2026.
retail_take: Routine share buyback continuation under existing authorization; modest repurchase volume suggests measured capital allocation. Market likely treats this as non-event absent broader strategic signals.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: Wise Group repurchased 1.03m shares for ~£6.3m across LSE and Nasdaq during 21-24 July as part of £405m buyback program.
summary: Wise Group PLC repurchased 1,028,515 Class A ordinary shares between 21-24 July 2026 through Goldman Sachs International: 648,736 shares on LSE at GBP 8.50-9.28, and 379,779 on Nasdaq at USD 11.41-12.49. Shares held in treasury. Execution forms part of announced £405m (≈$540m) buyback program. Detailed transaction-level data provided in compliance with MAR/UK FCA Listing Rules.
retail_take: Share buybacks typically signal management confidence in valuation and support EPS accretion, though this tranche represents modest progress (~0.1% of the program). Market likely to view neutrally absent broader strategic commentary.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: Kingfisher repurchased 11.9m shares at £2.95-£3.03 in week of 20-24 July as part of £300m buyback programme.
summary: Kingfisher PLC purchased 11.9 million ordinary shares for cancellation from Goldman Sachs International between 20-24 July 2026, at volume-weighted average prices ranging from £2.9469 to £2.9990 per share. This brings total purchases from GSI to 14.3 million shares under the second tranche of the company's £300 million share repurchase programme announced 24 March 2026. The company previously purchased 26.6 million shares from BNP Paribas under the first tranche. All purchases were on-exchange transactions on the London Stock Exchange.
retail_take: Routine capital allocation disclosure showing steady buyback execution within announced programme parameters. Share cancellation is modestly accretive to EPS but non-material to valuation. Non-event for most investors.

headline: Acceleration of Maddens development
brief: ECR Minerals redirects resources from Raglan to accelerate higher-grade Maddens development with trial alluvial mining at Brothers lease.
summary: ECR Minerals is redeploying operational personnel and mobile wash plant from Raglan to the Maddens Gold Project in North Queensland to commence trial alluvial mining at the Brothers mining lease. Surface prospecting indicates approximately 100,000 cubic metres of potentially minable material. Raglan transitions to geological evaluation and mine planning phase. The board views Maddens as the company's highest-priority development opportunity, with established mining leases and underground development already in place, positioning it as a near-term production asset.
retail_take: Market likely views positively as disciplined capital reallocation toward higher-potential asset with shorter production timeline, though Raglan pause suggests previous operations underperformed expectations.

headline: H1 2026 Trading Update
brief: Luceco reports H1 2026 revenue up 13% to £143m; confirms FY26 adjusted operating profit above £40m and raises FY27 guidance ahead of consensus.
summary: Luceco achieved H1 2026 revenue of £143m (up 13% YoY) with adjusted operating profit of £15.8m (up 14% YoY) at 11.1% margin. Energy Transition revenue surged 120% YoY while core products grew 6%. Bank net debt stands at £69.6m with leverage at 1.5x. The company confirms FY26 adjusted operating profit will exceed £40m and now expects FY27 adjusted operating profit to exceed current market consensus of £42.3m, though notes Demand Flexibility regulatory changes will moderate recurring EV charger revenue. CEO succession recruitment is progressing.
retail_take: Market likely positive; company beat H1 expectations, raised FY27 guidance ahead of consensus, and demonstrated pricing power despite commodity headwinds, though Demand Flexibility regulation creates some near-term headwind offset by core business resilience.

headline: Half-year Financial Report
brief: Coats delivers H1 organic growth of 1% amid market declines, maintains 19.8% EBIT margin, raises interim dividend 5%.
summary: Coats Group reported H1 2026 revenue of $837m, up 1% organically despite estimated mid-single digit market declines, demonstrating market outperformance. Adjusted EBIT of $166m maintained 19.8% margin including OrthoLite accretion. Apparel grew 1% organically; Footwear flat but accelerating in Q2. Free cash flow of $30m, net debt $842m (2.3x leverage, on track to 2.0x by year-end). Interim dividend increased 5% to 1.05c per share. Full-year outlook unchanged; company expects good earnings growth and strong free cash flow, with OrthoLite delivering $5m cost synergies in 2026 and $40m+ sales synergies by 2030.
retail_take: Positive signal: market share gains in weak conditions, margin resilience, and dividend growth backed by confident outlook suggest operational durability. OrthoLite integration tracking well with material upside potential. Full-year guidance confirmation de-risks stock.

headline: Major contract wins for Hudson Interxchange
brief: Hudson Interxchange secures major AI infrastructure contract and expansion order, bringing facility closer to breakeven.
summary: Hudson's New York data centre signed a five-year contract with a GPU cloud computing provider for 1.8MW capacity at 60 Hudson Street, with an additional 2MW right of first refusal. Billing commences September 2026 with 450kW initial deployment, full 1.35MW by year-end. Combined with an existing customer expansion order, contracted IT capacity on the sixth floor reaches approximately 2.8MW or 80% of 3.5MW saleable capacity. This positions Hudson significantly closer to breakeven and supports construction of final two data halls.
retail_take: Positive catalyst for CORD; validates Hudson's high-density AI/HPC strategy in Manhattan's most interconnected building, de-risks the facility's path to profitability, and demonstrates strong demand tailwinds for premium interconnect capacity.

headline: Lithium Ridge Grab Sample Results
brief: Andrada Mining extends Lithium Ridge mineralised trend by 50% to 9km; grab samples show high-grade lithium, tin and tantalum.
summary: Andrada Mining's 1,230 grab samples from Lithium Ridge in Namibia extended the mineralised trend from 6km to 9km. Results show 60 samples with lithium grades above 1% Li₂O, including 48 above 2%, with peak grades reaching 14.72% Li₂O. Additional polymetallic potential identified with 160 samples above 0.1% tin and 163 samples above 75ppm tantalum. Drilling programme of 16,500 metres completed in May 2026, with results pending. Work undertaken as Stage 1 of SQM partnership earn-in agreement.
retail_take: Positive indicators for exploration upside with expanded mineralisation and polymetallic potential, though subject to drill confirmation. Resource definition and commercial viability remain uncertain.

headline: Gorge Project – Nine Further Targets Identified
brief: GEO Exploration identifies nine additional exploration targets at Gorge Project in Western Australia, expanding portfolio to 12 ranked targets.
summary: Airborne geophysical surveys over the Gorge Project have confirmed the site is centred on the Wyloo Dome, a geological structure associated with major Australian gold deposits like Telfer and Fosterville. Nine new exploration targets were identified alongside upgrades to three existing rank-one targets: Gorge Mine, 401 Prospect, and MAG001. LiDAR data revealed 24 historic shafts and 12 trenches with extensive quartz veining, indicating more historical activity than previously known. The expanded target inventory and structural interpretation materially strengthen the company's geological model for gold mineralisation potential.
retail_take: Positive read: significantly expanded exploration pipeline with targets in a regionally significant geological setting comparable to major producing deposits; demonstrates de-risking through technical work and supports progression toward maiden drilling programme.

headline: Transaction in Own Shares
brief: Grafton Group purchases 59,528 shares at £9.53 average price as part of £25m buyback programme.
summary: On 27 July 2026, Grafton Group plc repurchased 59,528 ordinary shares for cancellation on the London Stock Exchange via Goodbody Stockbrokers at a volume-weighted average price of £9.5327, with trades ranging from £9.4740 to £9.6610. This brings total shares purchased under the £25m buyback announced 30 June 2026 to 1,198,700. The buyback programme continues alongside Deutsche Bank as intermediary.
retail_take: Routine share buyback execution within disclosed programme parameters. Signals capital deployment and potential EPS accretion but represents normal capital management activity; unlikely to move markets materially.

headline: Final Results
brief: NWF Group reports resilient FY26 results with revenue up 1.9% to £920.3m despite challenging market conditions. Dividend increased 3.6%.
summary: NWF Group delivered headline operating profit of £16.8m (up 3.1%) on revenue of £920.3m for year ended 31 May 2026. Food segment surged 19% to £5.1m profit; Fuels declined slightly to £8.1m amid heating oil demand weakness and Middle East volatility; Feeds stable at £3.6m. Net cash strengthened to £9.0m after acquiring two Fuels businesses for £4.8m. Total dividend increased to 8.7p (15th consecutive year of rises). Board expects current year performance broadly in line with FY26.
retail_take: Solid defensive performance in challenging conditions with strategic progress in Food and balanced sheet strengthening suggests cautious optimism; modest profit decline and muted outlook tempers enthusiasm but dividend growth signals management confidence.

headline: H1-26 Trading Update
brief: Creo Medical reports 45% H1 revenue growth to £3.2m, maintains FY guidance of 50-60% growth with lower costs.
summary: Creo Medical's H1-26 revenues increased 45% to £3.2m versus £2.2m prior year, with underlying operating costs down 15% to £7.8m and operating loss reduced 25% to £4.9m. The company completed manufacturing disposal and raised £5.5m equity plus £2m convertible loan in May 2026. Cash stood at £7.4m (down from £12.4m at year-end 2025) with further proceeds expected from pending 49% stake sale in Q3-26. Board maintains confidence in delivering full-year revenue growth of 50-60%, supported by strong order book, typical H2-weighted profile, and LATAM expansion.
retail_take: Positive momentum with tangible progress on costs and guidance reaffirmation, though cash burn and reliance on stake sale completion for funding runway warrant attention.

headline: Results for the six months ended 30 June 2026
brief: Croda delivers 4.6% organic sales growth and 6.7% profit growth in H1 2026, maintaining full-year guidance amid geopolitical uncertainty.
summary: Croda International reported H1 2026 sales of £880.5m (up 2.9% reported, 4.6% organic) with adjusted operating profit of £155.8m, up 6.7% organically. Consumer Care drove growth at +8%, with Beauty Actives surging 19%, while Life Sciences was flat and Industrial Specialties declined 2%. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 17.7% from 17.2%, benefiting from transformation savings (£18m incremental) and innovation focus. Free cash flow jumped 36.8% to £38.3m. The company maintained unchanged FY2026 guidance for 3-6% organic sales growth and margin expansion, targeting £100m efficiency benefits by FY2028.
retail_take: Solid execution on growth and margin expansion with strong momentum in Consumer Care offsetting Life Sciences weakness; unchanged guidance and disciplined capital allocation suggest confidence, but geopolitical headwinds and flat pharma sales warrant caution.

headline: Audited Final Results
brief: DSW Capital reports FY26 results with revenue up 27% to £6.2m, though adjusted PBT margin fell to 21.2% from 32.4% due to lower M&A activity.
summary: DSW Capital's year ended 31 March 2026 saw total income rise to £6.3m from £5.0m, driven by DR Solicitors' 12% annualised growth following its November 2024 acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA fell to £1.67m from £1.79m while adjusted PBT dropped to £1.31m from £1.57m, reflecting weaker M&A deal flow in the DSW Network caused by geopolitical uncertainty. The company generated strong operating cash of £1.82m (109% conversion), maintained £2.0m cash, and proposed a final dividend of 2.0p per share. Management highlighted improved diversification with M&A now 31% of income versus 55% prior year, plus strategic progress on DSW Legal launch and network expansion.
retail_take: Mixed signals: revenue growth and diversification are positive, but margin compression and falling PBT offset gains. The dividend hold and strong cash generation suggest confidence, but macro headwinds and declining profitability metrics may concern growth investors despite management optimism.

headline: Offeror Financing Update re Market Purchases
Unaudited Interim Results
brief: Staffline reports strong H1 2026 with revenue up 15.2% and operating profit surging 57.6%, guidance towards top end of market expectations.

headline: Q3 Trading Update
brief: SSP Group reports Q3 LFL sales growth of 4%, on track for full-year targets despite Middle East conflict impact.
summary: SSP Group achieved 4% constant currency sales growth in Q3 (April-June 2026) with matching LFL growth. Nine-month LFL sales also grew 5%. APAC & EEME contracted 2% LFL as Gulf markets traded at 65% of prior-year levels due to Middle East conflict. Group remains on track for full-year EPS of 13.6-14.8p, free cash flow above £100m, and ROCE progress toward 20% target. Share buyback completion stands at £76m of £100m initiated.
retail_take: Solid underlying trading momentum offset by geopolitical headwinds in Gulf; management guidance maintained suggests confidence in guidance achievability, though Middle East uncertainty remains a risk factor investors will monitor.

headline: Bakers Gold Heritage Agreement Signed
brief: Sunrise Resources secures heritage agreement clearing way for Baker's Gold exploration licence in Western Australia.
summary: Sunrise Resources has signed a heritage agreement with Yugunga-Nya Native Title Aboriginal Corporation, resolving a two-year dispute that will allow the company's Prospecting Licence 51/3378 application to be granted within weeks. Previous drilling at the Baker's Gold Project in Western Australia's Murchison Region intersected high-grade gold mineralisation: hole 21SBRC002 returned 2m grading 14.4g/t gold from 64m depth, with a 1m interval grading 26.51g/t gold. The mineralisation is open in all directions beneath an extensive gold-in-soil anomaly. The agreement establishes cooperation and heritage protection frameworks.
retail_take: Market likely views positively: removes regulatory hurdle to exploration restart on high-grade intercepts in a productive goldfield. However, stock appears thinly traded micro-cap; impact depends on execution and market sentiment toward junior explorers.

headline: Half Year results for the period ended 30 June

Core management fee EPS grew 46% to 12.4¢, while core performance fees surged to $207m from $67m year-on-year, reflecting broad-based contributions. Core profit before tax reached $297m with 35% margin. The firm recommended an interim dividend of 5.7¢ per share and completed $29m of a $50m share buyback programme.
retail_take: Strong operational momentum across diversified strategies with outperforming net inflows and shareholder-friendly capital allocation supports positive market reception, though absolute valuations and macro uncertainty warrant investor caution.

headline: 1H2026 Trading Update
brief: Winking Studios reports 20%+ revenue growth in 1H2026 but EBITDA margin compression due to strategic investments.

Adjusted EBITDA declined to $1.0-1.3m from $2.4m as the company invested ~$0.4m in North America studio Ampera (acquired April 2026) and ~$0.9m diverting resources to AI-enabled game development capabilities. 2H2026 revenue expected to exceed 1H results with continued investment planned.
retail_take: Growth trajectory is solid but near-term profitability pressure from M&A integration and capability-building investments may disappoint near-term margin-focused investors, though management frames these as positioning for higher-margin future opportunities.

headline: Trading Update
brief: Everplay Group reiterates FY26 guidance of £175.3m revenue and £50.7m adjusted EBITDA, with H2-weighted delivery ahead of major game releases.

summary: GreenRoc Strategic Materials has commenced Phase III drilling at its Amitsoq graphite deposit in South Greenland. The company plans drilling through August, with geotechnical and hydrogeological testing underway to support a Pre-Feasibility Study later this year. Amitsoq holds a 23.05Mt JORC resource at 20.41% graphite grade.
retail_take: Successful confirmation of ore continuity at expected grades represents on-track project development and validates exploration assumptions; positive momentum for a strategically designated EU project with secured financing and licensing in place.
